x: It was a pity that Mick Porter had to retire with shoe trouble as with 11 men in the first 81 positions he could have walked round to finish last and we should still have won the “Colman” Cup, which is awarded to the team with the lowest score for its complete team of 12 men. Reg Bolam, Eric Herbert, B.
Positions of our men were—4, Tobin; 5, McDonald; 8, Stimpson; 10, Whitehead; 14, Penstone. In the Mitcham A.C. 15 miles open road race we had quite a good number of our members competing and B.
With Braughton not eligible for a championship placing, owing to the fact that he is only 2nd claim to us, this meant that John Bromley took second place with Archie Bedford third. B.

In the circumstances, our 7th position in the team race was quite good and 22 clubs closed in. Pete Newell was our first man home in 16th place, and then came Bob Taylor 30th, Len Bishop 31st, Mike Stearman 62nd, B.

Our "A" team put up a very good performance to come home in first place out of a field of 33 teams, even though we were only placed 13th at the end of the first stage. "Ginger" Newell took us up into 5th place on the 2nd relay and we then had Ken Stimpson 7th, B.
Gawler, our friend from New Zealand, but as he was in our “ B ” team he could not score for our first team and our next two scoring men were B.
